name: Cryptid
shortDesc: Production-grade CLI cryptographic toolkit with AES-256-GCM and Argon2id. Secure by default, cross-platform.
fullDesc: Cryptid is a CLI-first cryptographic toolkit built with Python 3.13+. It provides secure text and file encryption/decryption using AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption with Argon2id key derivation. Designed to be secure by default and cross-platform.
challenges: Designing a secure file format that's self-describing
Argon2id is slow in tests — needed lower params for fixtures
Ensuring nonce uniqueness across all encryption operations
lessons: A writer should write, not transform — storage layer must not re-encrypt
Argon2id (256MB) is slow in tests — use lower params for test fixtures
Deduplication is critical — same insights appear across multiple sessions
architecture:
CLI (Typer + Rich)
  → Services (Encrypt, Decrypt, Folder, Key)
    → Crypto (CipherEngine, KDFEngine, KeyManager)
      → Storage (Reader, Writer)
        → Models (EncryptedFileHeader)

name: RPG-Game
shortDesc: Terminal-based RPG with turn-based combat, skill trees, inventory system, equipment rarities, and SQLite persistence.
fullDesc: A terminal-based RPG built entirely with Python. Features turn-based combat with a shield mechanic, dodge system, status effects, and spell casting. Includes skill trees for character progression, an inventory system with equipment rarities from Common to Mythic, and SQLite-based save persistence with atomic transactions and legacy JSON migration.
challenges: SQLite schema migration from legacy JSON saves
lessons: Property setters can cause subtle bugs with computed properties
SQLite transactions prevent data loss on crash
Mutable default arguments are a common source of bugs
future: Boss stat scaling by player level
architecture:
Game (orchestrator)
  → GameContext (DI container)
    → Combat, Player, Enemy, SkillTree
    → Inventory, QuestSystem, LootEngine
    → SaveSystem (SQLite)

name: QRGen
shortDesc: Terminal QR code generator with Unicode block rendering, ASCII fallback mode, and automatic terminal size validation.
fullDesc: A terminal QR code generator that renders QR codes directly in your terminal using Unicode block characters for clean, readable output. Includes an ASCII fallback mode for terminals without Unicode support, automatic terminal size validation to ensure the QR code fits, and configurable error correction levels.
challenges: Terminal size detection varies across platforms
Unicode support is inconsistent across terminals
Balancing QR code density with terminal width constraints
lessons: Environment variables need careful handling in shell commands
Terminal size detection is trickier than expected across platforms
Unicode support varies wildly — always provide ASCII fallbacks
QR code generation is more complex than it looks
architecture:
CLI (Typer + Rich)
  → QRGenerator (core logic)
    → Encoder (data → QR matrix)
    → Renderer (matrix → Unicode/ASCII)
    → TerminalValidator (size check)
    → ErrorCorrection (L/M/Q/H levels)

name: NoteApp
shortDesc: Desktop note-taking application with clean architecture, search functionality, and organized note management.
fullDesc: A desktop note-taking application built with Python and clean architecture principles. Features organized note management with categories, full-text search, and a structured approach to data persistence. Built to practice separation of concerns and maintainable GUI application design.
challenges: Implementing efficient full-text search without a database
lessons: Desktop UX requires fundamentally different thinking than CLI
File organization matters enormously as projects grow
Search is a feature users expect by default
Auto-save is harder than it looks
architecture:
GUI Layer (Tkinter/Custom)
  → Application (controller/mediator)
    → Services (NoteService, SearchService)
      → Repositories (NoteRepository)
        → Storage (JSON file persistence)
          → Models (Note, Category)

name: Merchant of the Realm
shortDesc: Medieval market tycoon CLI simulation game. Build a trading empire across towns with dynamic economy, NPCs, and caravans.
fullDesc: A CLI simulation game where you build a trading empire in a medieval kingdom. Buy low, sell high, manage workers, expand to multiple towns, and deal with dynamic weather, seasons, and random events. Built with Python 3.13+, Typer, and Rich — featuring a full save/load system, data-driven world generation, and a 24-phase development roadmap from MVP to endgame content.
features: Buy & sell goods across a dynamic market
Save/load game system with multiple slots
Calendar, tick system, and daily updates
Data-driven items, buildings, events, and NPC traits
Rich terminal UI with tables, panels, and colors
challenges: Designing a balanced economy that feels alive
Data-driven architecture for easy content expansion
lessons: Simulation games need careful balancing of reward loops
Data-driven design makes content iteration much faster
Save/load systems need to be designed early, not bolted on
architecture:
main.py (CLI entry)
  → Game Loop (menu, new game, load)
    → Core (state, config, save, logging)
    → Economy (market, pricing, trade)
    → World (generator, weather, events)
    → UI (renderer, panels, tables)
    → Data (JSON-driven items, buildings, NPCs)
